en: Jose Rizal was exiled to Dapitan, Zamboanga del Norte, for four years before his execution.
The Philippine eagle, also called the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and features a distinctive shaggy crest.
Carved into the mountains of Ifugao over 2,000 years ago, the Banaue Rice Terraces are a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, is the highest court and head of the judicial branch.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Hanunuo Mangyan of Mindoro preserve an ancient pre-colonial syllabic writing system that is still actively used and carved on bamboo today.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a two-step forward, one-step backward dance.
Filipino pediatrician Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines and was the first woman accepted to Harvard Medical School.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, with Tagalog, Cebuano, and Ilocano being among the most widely spoken native tongues.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his famous Spoliarium painting.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is symbolized by neighbors helping a family physically move their entire nipa hut.
